Surah An-Najm (The Star) [Meccan, and its verses are sixty-two]

﴿By the star﴾ (al-Najm), i.e., the Pleiades (al-Thurayya), ﴿when it sets﴾, i.e., disappears.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 53, verse 2:

﴿Your companion has not strayed﴾ Muhammad, upon him be blessings and peace, from the path of guidance, ﴿nor has he erred﴾, meaning he has not been involved in error (ghayy), which is ignorance arising from corrupt belief.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 53, verse 3:

﴿Nor does he speak from [his own] desire.﴾ He does not speak about what he brings to you out of his own desire (hawa nafsihi).
﴿In﴾ it is not ﴿but a revelation that is revealed﴾ to him.
﴿He was taught it﴾ by an angel.

ذُو مِرَّة (possessor of strength): quwwa wa shidda (strength and vehemence), or manzar hasan (a fine appearance); i.e., Jibril, upon him be peace. فاسْتَوى (and he stood firm/poised): istaqarra (he settled).

Note on the translation: the source text is Tafsir al-Jalalayn's gloss on this verse, and I have rendered it as it stands.

Translation:

﴿Possessor of strength﴾: quwwa (strength) and shidda (vehemence), or manzar hasan (a good appearance), i.e., Jibril, upon him be peace. ﴿And he stood firm﴾: istaqarra (he settled, became steady).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 7:

﴿And he was on the highest horizon﴾ the horizon of the sun, i.e., at its rising, in his original form in which he was created. The Prophet ﷺ saw him, and he was at Hira', and [Jibril] had filled the horizon to the west, so he fell down unconscious. He had asked him to show himself to him in his original form in which he was created, so he promised him at Hira', and Jibril descended to him in the form of the sons of Adam.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 53, verse 8:

﴿Then he drew near﴾ — he came close to him — ﴿and descended﴾ — he increased in nearness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 9:

﴿Then he was﴾ from Him ﴿at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer﴾ than that, until he regained consciousness and his fright subsided.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 10:

﴿So He revealed﴾ (Exalted is He) ﴿to His servant﴾ Jibril ﴿that which He revealed﴾ Jibril conveyed to the Prophet ﷺ, and He did not mention what was revealed, out of glorification of its importance.

﴿Mā kadhaba﴾ (The heart did not lie about) with a light or a doubled pronunciation of the letter *dhāl* (*takhfīf wa-tashdīd*), meaning it denied (*ankara*) ﴿al-fu'ād﴾ (the heart), the heart of the Prophet, ﴿mā ra'ā﴾ (what it saw) with his eyes, of the form of Jibrīl (Gabriel).
﴿Will you then dispute with him﴾ — you argue with him and overcome him — ﴿about what he sees?﴾ — an address to the polytheists who deny the Prophet's ﷺ seeing of Jibril.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 13:**

﴿Indeed, he saw him﴾ in his (true) form, ﴿another time﴾, once.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 14:

﴿Near the Lote-tree of the utmost boundary﴾ when he was taken on the Night Journey through the heavens; it is a lote-tree (sidr) on the right of the Throne, which none of the angels or others may pass beyond.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 15:

﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾. The angels take refuge in it, and so do the spirits of the martyrs and of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun).

When ﴿إذْ﴾ (idh) means "when," and it governs ﴿رَآهُ﴾ (ra'ahu, "he saw him"). ﴿Ideh covers the lote-tree (al-sidrah) with what covers it﴾ means: of birds and other things.

Correction to my rendering above: the Qur'anic words should read, in plain English translation: "When there covered the lote-tree that which covered it."

Clean translation of the passage:

When ﴿idh﴾ means "when," and it governs ﴿ra'ahu﴾ ("he saw him"). ﴿When there covered the lote-tree that which covered it﴾ means: of birds and other things.
﴿The eye did not swerve﴾ from the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿nor did it transgress﴾, meaning: his eye did not turn away from the thing intended for it to see, nor did it go beyond that during that night.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 53, verse 18:

﴿Indeed he saw﴾ in that night ﴿of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾, the great ones, meaning some of them. He saw among the wonders of the malakut (the unseen dominion of God) a green rafraf (a green cushion or canopy) that filled the horizon of the sky, and Jibril (Gabriel) had six hundred wings.

**﴿And Manāt, the third, the other one﴾** — "the other one" is a term of disparagement applied to the third (idol), while the two before it are al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā. It was an idol of stone that the polytheists worshipped, and they claimed that it would intercede for them with Allah. The first object of *afa-ra'aytum* ("have you considered?") is *al-Lāt* and what is conjoined to it, and the second object is omitted; the meaning is: "Tell me, do these idols have any power over anything, that you worship them besides Allah, who is capable of what has been mentioned before?" Also, when they claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah, despite their own dislike of daughters, this was revealed.
﴿Unjust﴾, from "ḍāzahu yaḍīzuhu," meaning when he wronged him and oppressed him.

﴿They are only﴾, that is, the things mentioned, ﴿names you and your fathers have named﴾, that is, you named idols with them, which you worship, ﴿for which God has sent down no authority﴾, that is, no authorization for worshipping them, ﴿no proof or evidence﴾. ﴿They follow only conjecture and what their souls desire﴾, that is, in their worship of them, what Satan made attractive to them, namely that these idols would intercede for them with God Most High. ﴿Yet guidance has already come to them from their Lord﴾ through the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ), with the decisive proof, ﴿but they did not turn away from what they were upon﴾.
﴿Or does man have whatever he wishes?﴾ That is, for every one of them ﴿whatever he wishes﴾ of the notion that the idols will intercede for them? ﴿The matter is not so.﴾
﴿So to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾, i.e., the worldly life, so nothing happens in either of them except what He, exalted is He, wills.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (*Tafsir al-Jalalayn*, the *tafsir* or exegesis) on Surah 53, verse 26:**

﴿And how many an angel there is in the heavens﴾, meaning, many of the angels, and how noble they are with Allah, ﴿whose intercession avails nothing except after Allah gives permission for them to intercede for whomever He wills of His servants﴾, ﴿and is pleased with﴾ him, in accordance with His saying, ﴿And they do not intercede except for one whom He approves﴾. It is known that their intercession does not occur except after permission is given for it: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾
﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with the names of females.﴾ That is, they said: they are the daughters of God.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 53, verse 28:

﴿And they have no knowledge of it﴾, of this statement, ﴿they follow only conjecture﴾ which they have imagined in it, ﴿and conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾, meaning, it does not suffice in place of knowledge in matters where knowledge is what is required.

﴿So turn away from those who turn away from Our remembrance﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and desire nothing but the worldly life﴾. And this was before the command concerning jihad (struggle, including armed fighting).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 30:

﴿That﴾, i.e., the pursuit of the worldly life, ﴿is the extent of their knowledge﴾, i.e., the limit of their knowledge is that they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided﴾, knowing both of them, so He will recompense them both.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 31:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.﴾ He is the Owner of that. From Him comes the one who goes astray and the one who is guided: He sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. ﴿That He may recompense those who did evil with what they had done﴾ of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and other than it, ﴿and recompense those who did good﴾ with tawhid (affirming the oneness of Allah) and other than it of acts of obedience, ﴿with the best (al-husna)﴾, which is Paradise. And He described the good-doers with His saying:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 32:

﴿Those who avoid the major sins and the abominations, except for minor faults (al-lamam)﴾ are the small sins, such as a glance, a kiss, and a touch. So it is an exceptive clause of a disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), and the meaning is: but minor faults are forgiven through avoiding the major sins. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾ through that, and through accepting repentance. It was revealed concerning those who used to say: "Our prayer, our fasting, our pilgrimage." ﴿He knows best﴾, i.e., He is Knowing ﴿about you, when He produced you from the earth﴾, i.e., He created your father Adam from dust, ﴿and when you were embryos﴾, the plural of janin (embryo), ﴿so do not claim purity for yourselves﴾, do not praise them out of self-admiration; but if it is by way of acknowledging the blessing, then it is good. ﴿He knows best﴾, i.e., He is Knowing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 33:

﴿Have you considered the one who turned away﴾ from the faith, and apostatized when he was reproached for it, and said: "Indeed I feared the punishment of Allah." So the one who reproached him guaranteed for him that he would bear Allah's punishment on his behalf if he returned to his polytheism, and he gave him such-and-such of his wealth, and so he returned.

﴿And gave a little﴾ of the wealth mentioned, ﴿and withheld﴾ the rest. It is derived from *al-kadiyya* (a hard ground, like a rock, that stops the well-digger's spade when he reaches it while digging).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 35:

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾ He knows from it (that is, from the unseen) that another will bear his punishment in the Hereafter? No. He is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira or someone else. The clause "a'indahu" (does he have) is the second object of "ra'ayta" (have you seen), in the sense of "akhbirni" (tell me).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 36:

﴿Am﴾ (rather, "or"): ﴿has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Musa﴾ (the books of the Torah) ﴿or the scrolls before it﴾ (the earlier scriptures)

﴿And﴾ the scrolls of ﴿Abraham, who fulfilled [his trust]﴾. [He] completed what he was commanded to do, such as ﴿And when Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them﴾, and the explanation of what

﴿أ﴾ أنْ ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ إلَخْ (etc.). وأَنْ مُخَفَّفَة مِن الثَّقِيلَة (wa-anna mukhaffafa min al-thaqila, meaning: the particle أنْ here is the lightened form of the heavy anna, i.e., of إنّ with its emphatic force) أيْ (that is) لا تَحْمِل نَفْس ذَنْب غَيْرها (no soul shall bear the sin of another).

Here is the translation:

﴿And﴾ meaning: that ﴿there is not for man except what he strives for﴾ of good; so he has no good from the striving of another.
﴿And that his effort will be seen﴾ it will be seen in the Hereafter.

Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense. Al-Ak'mal (the most complete): it is said, "I repaid him his effort" and "I repaid him for his effort."

Note on the translation: the passage is a short gloss from al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti on the Qur'anic phrase ﴿ثُمَّ يُجْزاهُ الجَزاء الأَوْفى﴾ (Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense), explaining the word al-awfa as al-akmal (the most complete) and giving two grammatical usages of the verb jaza.

وَأَنَّ (wa-anna), with fatḥa, as a conjunction (ʿatfan) linking it to what precedes; it is also read with kasra as a new sentence (istiʾnafan), and likewise what follows it, so on the second reading the content of these clauses is not in the scrolls. ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾, the return and the destination after death, so that He will recompense them.
﴿And that it is He who makes laugh﴾ whom He wills, makes him glad, ﴿and makes weep﴾ whom He wills, makes him sad.
And that it is He who causes death in the world, and gives life for the resurrection.
﴿And that He created the two mates﴾ the two kinds (al-sinfayn)

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 53, verse 46:

﴿from a drop﴾ of semen (manī), ﴿when it is emitted﴾, poured into the womb.

ﾠ﻿"And that it is He Who brings about the second creation" (al-nash'ah al-ukhra), pronounced with madd and with qasr, "the second creation": the second act of creating, for resurrection after the first creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 48:

﴿And that it is He who makes rich﴾ people with sufficiency through wealth, ﴿and grants possessions﴾ He gave wealth that is taken as a store of property (qinyah).

And that He is the Lord of Sirius (al-Shi'ra).

It is a star behind Orion (al-Jawza'), which was worshipped in the pre-Islamic period (al-Jahiliyyah).

﴿And that He destroyed ʿĀd, the first﴾. And in another reading, the nunation is assimilated into the lām and it is pronounced with a ḍammah without a hamzah (al-Ūlā, with the tanwīn of ʿĀdan merged into the lām). They are the people of ʿĀd, and "the other" (al-Ukhrā) refers to the people of Ṣāliḥ.

﴿And Thamud﴾ with ṣarf (تنوين الصرف, the nunation that marks full declension) is the name of the forefather, and without ṣarf (بِلا صَرْف) it is the name of the tribe. It is conjoined to ʿĀdan (ʿĀd), ﴿and He spared none﴾ of them, not one.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 52:

﴿And the people of Nuh before [them]﴾: i.e., before ʿAad and Thamud, whom We destroyed. ﴿Indeed, they were more unjust and more transgressing﴾ than ʿAad and Thamud, due to the long duration of Nuh's stay among them. ﴿And he remained among them a thousand years, less fifty years﴾. And they, along with their disbelief in him, would harm him and beat him.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** (the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 53 (al-Najm), verse 53:

﴿And the overturned cities﴾ — these are the settlements of the people of Lut (Lot). ﴿He threw them down﴾ — He brought them down after lifting them up to the sky, overturning them toward the earth by His command, (carried out by) Jibril (Gabriel) for this purpose.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 54:

﴿So there covered them﴾ of the stones after that ﴿that which covered﴾. It is left vague for awe-inspiring effect. And in Hud (Surah 11): ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of hardened clay﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 55:

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord⁠ will you doubt⁠﴾ their blessings that indicate His oneness and His power. ﴿Will you doubt⁠﴾ will you be skeptical, O man, or deny?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 56:

﴿This﴾ [i.e., Muhammad] ﴿is a warner of the warners of old﴾, of their kind, meaning a messenger like the messengers before him, sent to you just as they were sent to their peoples.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 57:

﴿The approaching one has approached﴾ the Resurrection has drawn near.

﴿There is none besides Allah to disclose it﴾ — a soul. ﴿Except Him, none can reveal it﴾ — meaning, none disclosing or manifesting it except Him, like His saying: ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 53, verse 59:

﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse?﴾ That is, the Qur'an. ﴿You laugh at it﴾ in denial.

Translation:

﴿And you laugh﴾ mockingly, ﴿and do not weep﴾ at hearing its promise and its warning.
﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾ (heedless, unmindful, neglectful of what is required of you).
﴿So prostrate to Allah﴾ who created you, ﴿and worship [Him]﴾, and do not prostrate to the idols nor worship them.
